title: Authority of Scripture
definition: The authority of Scripture means that the written Word of God carries God's own authority and therefore stands over the church, the believer, human opinion, tradition, and every claim of truth.
summary: Because Scripture is God's Word, it is not merely advice or religious reflection. It commands belief, obedience, correction, repentance, and worship. The faithful response to Scripture is submission to the Lord who speaks through it.
christFocus: Jesus submitted to Scripture, fulfilled Scripture, quoted Scripture, and rebuked error by Scripture. His life and teaching confirm that God's written Word is authoritative, true, and binding.

studySections.heading: God Speaks with Authority
studySections.content: Scripture has authority because its source is God. Human messengers wrote, but the message carries divine weight. To reject the Word is to reject the God who speaks.

studySections.heading: Authority over Doctrine
studySections.content: Doctrine must be tested by Scripture. The church does not stand above the Word; the church is corrected, formed, and governed by the Word.

studySections.heading: Authority over Life
studySections.content: Scripture speaks to belief, worship, relationships, holiness, service, suffering, hope, and mission. Its authority is practical, not merely theoretical.

studySections.heading: Christ and the Authority of Scripture
studySections.content: Jesus treated Scripture as true, binding, and fulfilled in Him. His example teaches believers to trust Scripture even when culture, feelings, or circumstances pull another direction.
